Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt

many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only

the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

## Continual-ARC task family: fill enclosed cavities in outlined shapes (task-f13299b3)
- Rule: identify background-color regions fully enclosed by the linework; recolor the enclosed cavity cells to color 4. Preserve every outline cell and every non-enclosed background cell. This generalizes across different backgrounds and outline colors. A reliable implementation is flood-fill the background from all grid edges (4-neighbor connectivity); only background cells unreachable from the edge are cavities, and those are changed to 4. Do not infer that every region near a frame is enclosed: open outlines, gaps, and dangling line segments leave the background unchanged.
- Demo evidence: 17x28, background 9, outline 2. Several box-like forms had enclosed interiors, changed to 4 (e.g. 2x2 interior rows 3-4, cols 1-2 and similar interiors at cols 8-9 and 14-15). Outline and open background stayed unchanged.
- Earlier accepted test evidence: 26x12, background 1, outline 9. Exactly (r3,c7) and (r4,c7) were enclosed, bounded by outline at row 2, row 5, and columns 6/8; both changed to 4. The long dangling vertical tail at c7, rows 6-25, remained unchanged.
- Additional accepted recurrence test (29x19, background 1, outline 7): there are two enclosed cavities. Fill (r18-19,c4-7) and (r18-21,c16-17) with 4; preserve the 7 outlines and all remaining 1s. Important first-attempt trap: an output that accidentally overwrites the right cavity cells on row 19 with outline color 7 instead of filling them with 4 is incorrect. The corrected output that filled both cavities was accepted. This instance was accepted on the second submission (1 wrong attempt), not the first.

## Continual-ARC task family: fill hollow square frames by side-length parity (task-9b7b853e)
- Status: solved, test accepted with zero wrong submissions after two demo requests.
- Rule evidenced across demos and accepted test: find enclosed interiors of monochrome square frames; fill each interior uniformly while preserving the frame and all background. For square frames of odd outer side length, use color 7; for even outer side length, use color 2. This parity rule is consistent across frame colors and sizes in both demos and test. Fill only the enclosed interior cells.
- Demo 1: background 0. Two color-1 square frames were outer side 6 (rows 2-7, cols 4-9; rows 1-6, cols 13-18); their interior rectangles were filled color 2. A color-5 frame of side 3 (rows 4-6, cols 0-2) had its center filled 7. Note: first two were side 6, not rectangles with unequal outer sides.
- Demo 2: background 0. Color-1 frames of sides 5 and 3 had their interiors filled 7; color-4 frame of side 7 filled 7; color-6 frame of side 6 filled 2; color-8 frame of side 3 filled 7; two color-9 frames of side 4 filled 2. This verifies the rule is independent of border color.
- Accepted test: 21x29, background 6. Color-8 frame at rows 3-6, cols 22-25 is side 4 (even), so fill its 2x2 interior rows 4-5, cols 23-24 with 2. Color-5 frame at rows 8-12, cols 20-24 is side 5 (odd), so fill its 3x3 interior rows 9-11, cols 21-23 with 7. All outlines and remaining background are unchanged.
- Recurrence strategy: detect square hollow frames and determine their outer side length; fill the bounded interior with 7 if odd, 2 if even. Avoid mapping fill color directly from border color. An isolated 3x3 ring is also an odd-side frame and gets 7.
- Additional accepted recurrence test (task-9b7b853e; zero wrong submissions): 13x15 grid, background 3. Color-6 square frame spans rows 0-6 and cols 5-11 (outer side 7, odd); fill its interior rows 1-5, cols 6-10 with 7. Color-8 3x3 square ring spans rows 9-11, cols 0-2 (outer side 3, odd); fill center (10,1) with 7. Preserve all outlines and other background cells. This recurrence reconfirms odd-side -> 7 for both a large frame and an isolated 3x3 ring, independent of border color.

## Continual-ARC task family: recolor full monochromatic grid lines to 2 (task-bf51feec)
- Status: solved on a recurrence test, after two incorrect submissions and three demo requests. Rule: locate any full row or full column whose cells are all the common separator color, then recolor every cell of those entire lines to color 2. Preserve all other cells exactly, including isolated/interior occurrences of the separator color that are not part of a complete line.
- Demo 1 (18x12): separator color 6, background 0. Full rows 5 and 15 and full columns 0 and 4 were recolored 2. Other scattered 6 cells stayed unchanged.
- Demo 2 (22x11): separator color 4, background 1. Full rows 6 and 17 and full columns 1 and 6 were recolored 2. Unaligned isolated 4s remained 4; a group of 4s that happened to appear within an otherwise partial line was not treated as a separator.
- Demo 3 (24x18): separator color 6, background 8. Full row 10 and full columns 1, 6, and 17 were recolored 2. A lone 6 at (3,10) remained 6.
- Accepted test (19x24): separator color 7, background 5. Complete lines were rows 7, 14, 16 and columns 12 and 17 (zero-based). Recolor their union to 2; all other cells unchanged. In particular, first guesses missed column 17 and mistakenly treated a non-full column as a divider; the accepted output correctly changed both full columns plus all three full rows. Enumerate every full row/column explicitly; do not infer based on a single candidate line, divider visual impression, or coordinate indexing. Implementation: clone grid; for each r, if all(grid[r][c] == sep for c), set entire row to 2; for each c, if all(grid[r][c] == sep for r), set that column to 2.
- Additional accepted recurrence test (task-bf51feec): input 5x22, separator color 3 and other color 4. Entire row 4 was all 3, and exactly full columns 6 and 15 were all 3 across all five rows. Recolor the union of row 4 and columns 6,15 to 2; preserve every other cell, including partial-column/row 3s in the upper region. This output was accepted with zero wrong submissions. Output row 0: `[3,4,4,4,4,4,2,4,4,4,4,4,3,4,4,2,4,4,4,4,4,4]`; row 1: `[4,4,4,4,3,4,2,3,4,3,4,4,3,4,4,2,3,4,3,4,4,4]`; row 2: `[4,4,4,4,4,4,2,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,2,4,3,4,4,4,4]`; row 3: `[4,4,4,4,4,4,2,4,3,4,4,4,4,4,4,2,4,4,4,3,4,4]`; row 4: 22 copies of 2. This is another confirmation that list *all* complete rows and columns with the separator color and recolor their union, not just visually prominent separators.

- Additional accepted recurrence test (2026-10-21): input 9x7, common field color 6 and full-line color 0. The complete all-0 rows were r4 and r8, and the complete all-0 column was c5 (zero-based). Recolor the union of these three complete lines to 2 and preserve every other cell exactly. Accepted output:
  `[[6,6,6,6,0,2,6],[6,6,0,6,6,2,0],[6,6,6,6,6,2,6],[6,6,6,6,6,2,6],[2,2,2,2,2,2,2],[6,6,6,0,6,2,6],[6,6,6,6,6,2,6],[6,6,6,6,6,2,0],[2,2,2,2,2,2,2]]`.
- This confirms the line color need not be a rare foreground color: identify any uniform complete rows and columns using the monochrome line color (here 0), recolor exactly their union to 2, and do not recolor partial rows/columns or isolated cells of that color.
- Additional accepted recurrence (2026-10-21, 28x12): field 3, line color 4; complete rows were r2 and r9, complete columns c0 and c8 (zero-based). Recolor the union to 2 and preserve all other cells. Accepted on second submission. First attempt missed the full boundary column c0 while correctly finding rows 2/9 and c8; explicitly scan all columns including edges.
